business_summary.text: Urban Company operates an online marketplace for at-home consumer services in India, the UAE and Singapore, sells Native-branded water purifiers and smart locks, and runs InstaHelp housekeeping.

call_points.text: Total orders 13.2 million, up 79% YoY; 1.2 million new customers added, first quarter above one million.
India Consumer Services marketing spend was ₹25 Cr versus ₹24 Cr a year ago, so growth came without more marketing.
Native M3 water purifier launched with three-year no-service promise; Native may add at most one more category in five years.
Cash and treasury investments of ₹2,019 Cr, down only about ₹2 Cr from the prior quarter.
InstaHelp training capacity is stretched: supply addition is outpacing trainers and training rooms.
No new international markets planned; focus stays on India, UAE, Singapore and the Saudi JV.
More than 90-95% of code is now written by AI, with leverage showing in engineering costs and headcount.
Management retains targets of consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28 and ₹1,000 Cr by FY31.
India Consumer Services ex-InstaHelp Q4 revenue grew 26% to ₹808 Cr with EBITDA margin at 3.3% of NTV.
Native Q4 NTV grew 67% YoY to ₹89 Cr, while full-year adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed from ₹39 Cr to ₹31 Cr.

operating_notes.text: GST show cause dated May 04, 2026 demands ₹8,70,03,806 including interest and penalty for April 2022 to March 2023, on alleged GSTR-1 vs GSTR-3B turnover differences and excess ITC.
Q4FY26 other expenses of ₹321.86 Cr were 38.6% above Q3FY26's ₹232.26 Cr, the largest driver of the quarter's loss.
FY26 EBITDA margin was -14.33%, versus -9.6% for 9MFY26, so margins deteriorated in the March quarter.
FY26 InstaHelp NTV was ₹79 Cr with an Adjusted EBITDA loss of ₹235 Cr; Q4 alone had 2.67 million orders and ₹40.1 Cr NTV.
FY26 India Consumer Services (Ex-InstaHelp) Adjusted EBITDA was ₹131 Cr, 4.1% of NTV, versus 3.3% in FY25.
FY26 International (Ex-KSA) NTV was ₹700 Cr (+75% YoY) with Adjusted EBITDA of ₹6 Cr; KSA JV NTV ₹175 Cr with UC's share of loss ₹31.17 Cr.
Q4FY26 consolidated NTV grew 42% YoY to ₹1,148 Cr.
Q1FY27 InstaHelp delivered 3.82 million orders with an Adjusted EBITDA loss of ₹132 Cr and loss per order of ₹346.
Q1FY27 India Consumer Services marketing spend was ₹25 Cr versus ₹24 Cr a year earlier.
About 75% of early Native water-purifier cohorts are renewing filters through the company.
Q2FY27 other income includes ₹7.68 Cr insurance settlement for inventory destroyed in the Bhiwandi fire of May 12, 2025, against a ₹9.11 Cr loss booked in FY26.
H1FY27 share-based payment expense was ₹94.19 Cr versus ₹48.11 Cr a year earlier.
The ESOP Trust transferred 2,06,11,561 equity shares in H1FY27 on exercise of options under ESOP-2015.
InstaHelp fulfilled orders 6.2 million in Q2FY27, up 63% QoQ, with NOV down to ₹114 from ₹138.
India Consumer Services had ~57k monthly active service partners in Q2FY27, up 16.1% YoY; partners earned ₹30,708 per month in H1FY27 on 97 utilised hours.
Voice AI volumes grew from 0.5 million minutes in Q4FY26 to 14.3 million in Q2FY27.
India Consumer Services NTV grew 26.3% YoY to ₹963 Cr with Adjusted EBITDA of ₹34 Cr (3.5% of NTV).
International NTV grew 66% YoY to ₹267 Cr; KSA JV NTV ₹93 Cr, loss narrowed to ₹(16) Cr.
Native NTV grew 35% YoY to ₹132 Cr; RO ASPs rose 4.3% QoQ with filter attach ~75%.
H1FY27 NTV reached ₹2,897 Cr, up 40.6% YoY.

timeline.summary: Urban Company Limited’s Board of Directors will hold a meeting on May 08, 2026, to approve audited standalone and consolidated financial results for Q4FY26 and FY26 ending March 31, 2026.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹425.56 Cr, net loss ₹161.16 Cr.
FY26 annual report: consolidated revenue ₹1,555.54 Cr (+36%), net loss ₹234.81 Cr after a ₹61 Cr deferred-tax write-down, unmodified audit opinion, ₹116.69 Cr contingent liabilities.
Urban Company reported Q4 FY26 consolidated NTV growth of 42% YoY to ₹1,148 Cr and revenue of ₹426 Cr, with core business expansion offsetting heavy investments in InstaHelp.
In May 2026, Urban Company received a stamp duty and penalty order totaling ~₹0.49 crore from the Delhi authorities, which is already under challenge via a writ petition in the Delhi High Court.
In May 2026, Urban Company announced that the Chennai GST department dropped its ₹8.70 Cr show-cause notice proceedings with zero penalty.
In June 2026, Urban Company announced the cancellation of the commercial registration for its Saudi Arabian step-down subsidiary, UC KSA.
Urban Company filed its FY26 annual report showing revenue of ₹1,556 Cr and net loss of ₹235 Cr with clean audit opinions.
